scenes.title: 1971 UCL & 2005 Trondheim 2-Meter Open Arena: Single-Corner 'Place Cell' Bullseye Beside the Honeycomb 'Hexagonal Grid Cell' Lattice
scenes.era: 1971 London & 2005 Trondheim Nobel Spatial Neuroscience Suite

layout.description: Sunlit high-key Nordic-British neurobiology room featuring a clean white **2-meter circular/square open-field arena** on a low platform with a bold white-and-black north landmark cue card on its rim, an **articulated matte-white porcelain rat sculpture** exploring smoothly across the floor, and a crisp dual-panel overhead trajectory display contrasting **Panel A: O'Keefe Place Cell (1 single warm-amber hotspot in the NW corner)** with **Panel B: Moser Grid Cell (crystal-symmetric 60° hexagonal honeycomb dots tiling the entire floor!)**.

positions.who: John O'Keefe (mannequin in smart tweed blazer over collared shirt)
positions.where: pointing on Display Panel A to the concentrated single-location firing zone in the arena's northwest quadrant

positions.who: May-Britt Moser & Edvard Moser (mannequins in crisp Scandinavian sweaters/blazers)
positions.where: pointing in delight on Display Panel B to the unmistakable 60-degree hexagonal honeycomb grid emerging across the expanded 2-meter arena
exploring freely across the clean white open-field arena toward the north cue card

props.name: 2-meter clean white open-field arena with rotatable visual cue card
props.period_detail: the enlarged floor that unmasked the repeating 60° hexagonal grid in 2005

props.name: articulated matte-white porcelain rat sculpture
props.period_detail: freely moving exploration (never strapped down!) was essential to discovering Place & Grid cells
props.physical_behavior: complies cleanly with R46 porcelain animal rule

props.name: Side-by-Side '1971 Place Cell (1 Spot)' vs '2005 Grid Cell (Hexagonal Lattice)' trajectory screens
props.period_detail: shows single pushpin vs full honeycomb coordinate paper in one glance

actions.verb_sequence: trots freely across the white 2-meter arena floor -> Panel A lights up strictly in the NW corner (Place Cell) while Panel B lights up at crisp 60-degree honeycomb vertices across the entire floor (Grid Cell)
rotates the arena's north cue card 90 degrees -> both spatial maps rotate 90 degrees in lockstep!

reactions.reaction: smile tracing the equilateral triangles connecting every firing vertex
nods seeing Tolman's 1948 'Cognitive Map' proven down to exact geometry

scenes.wardrobe: Academic tweed blazer and shirt; clean Scandinavian tailored knitwear and blazers.
scenes.recognition_hook: Make the arena floor big enough, and single brain cells spontaneously draw crystal-perfect 60-degree honeycomb graph paper across the room!

key_visual.description: a sunlit neurobiology lab with a 2-meter white open-field floor holding a matte-white porcelain rat sculpture beside dual trajectory screens comparing a single-spot Place Cell and a 60-degree hexagonal Grid Cell honeycomb

scenes.title: Why the Small Box Hid the Hexagon Until 2005

layout.description: Tabletop comparison of a cramped 70-cm box (cropping only 3 dots) beside the wide 200-cm enclosure (revealing 19 hexagonal vertices!).

positions.where: lifting away the small inner frame to reveal the full repeating honeycomb across the wide floor

props.name: 70-cm cropped frame vs 200-cm full hexagonal floor
props.period_detail: dramatic lesson in scaling experimental space to match biology

actions.verb_sequence: expand the enclosure walls -> partial dots snap into a unmistakable 60° crystal lattice

scenes.recognition_hook: Inside a tiny box it looked like three random blobs — widen the walls to two meters and a mathematical honeycomb jumps off the screen.

scenes.title: Building a 'Memory Palace' on Your Own Place Cells

layout.description: Sunlit room where a speaker walks mentally from front door -> sofa -> bookshelf -> window, anchoring one key speech topic at each physical landmark.

positions.where: walking calmly past four room landmarks reciting a 20-minute talk without notes

props.name: 4 room landmark anchor cards ('1. Door | 2. Sofa | 3. Shelf | 4. Window')
props.period_detail: puts ancient Method of Loci directly onto O'Keefe's Place Cells

actions.verb_sequence: touches each room spot mentally -> recalls every section in effortless sequence

scenes.recognition_hook: The 2,500-year-old Memory Palace trick works because your hippocampus remembers 'WHERE' ten times better than naked bullet lists.
